title: Re-authenticate before high-value changes (default: enabled)
context: A high-value change (password change, MFA change, session terminate, account delete) that runs on the same session that opened the surface is a phishing risk when the session is stale. WCAG 3.3.4 (Error Prevention on legal, financial and data-changing actions) applies. The spec section 5.4 marks reauth-window as elicited with recommendedDefault true, meaning re-authenticate is enabled by default.
decision: reauth-window is elicited as an enum owned by `blueprint.json.elicits[id=reauth-window].options`; the option vocabulary and recommended default are owned by that manifest elicit. A high-value change fires the re-authenticate flow when the session was last authenticated more than the elicited number of minutes ago; the `never` option disables the trigger for projects whose sessions themselves expire within minutes. The re-authenticate flow itself is owned by the applied auth blueprint; this ADR names the trigger, not the implementation.
consequences: A stolen laptop with an unlocked session cannot terminate every other session without re-authenticating within the elicited window. The re-authenticate cost is a modal prompt on the operators sessions view, not a full sign-out flow.

alternativesConsidered.name: Alternative approach considered
alternativesConsidered.summary: Always require re-authenticate was considered but every operators surface would trigger it; a windowed policy balances safety and workflow.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: See the decision text; the chosen shape composes cleanly with the applied blueprint set the spec section 5.4 names.
